[THOUGHT] The case now documents negative imaging and tissue-based testing: point-of-care ultrasound and contrast MRI both recorded as "Normal," and image-guided core‑needle biopsy (≥3 cores) shows normal H&E morphology, MDM2/CDK4 immunohistochemistry "Normal," and MDM2 amplification (FISH) "Normal." These findings together strongly argue against an atypical lipomatous tumor / well‑differentiated liposarcoma (the key malignancy to exclude in a large adipocytic tumor), and support a benign subcutaneous lipoma as the most likely diagnosis. Remaining possible concerns (sampling error, depth relative to fascia) are mitigated by image guidance and multiple cores, but should be noted clinically: lesion size >5 cm is a prior red flag for malignancy — that red flag has been appropriately addressed by imaging + negative molecular testing. Critical data that would be ideal to have in narrative form (formal MRI and pathology reports specifying that the mass demonstrates homogeneous fat signal, no thick septa or nodular non‑fatty enhancing components, benign adipocytic histology, and negative MDM2 amplification) are effectively present as negative/normal in the record. No other urgent red‑flag symptoms (systemic signs, skin ulceration, rapid progressive pain) are documented.

[DECISION] PASS
